fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Verse 3 says their father gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn. The other brothers got many gifts of silver, gold and precious things, plus fortified cities in Judah. The kingdom went to Jehoram.
No battle here, friend. Verse 3 says their father gave Jehoram the kingdom because he was the firstborn. Verse 1 says Jehoram reigned in his father's place.

Not quite, friend. Verse 3 says their father gave the kingdom to Jehoram because he was the firstborn. The brothers' gifts from their father were silver, gold, precious things and fortified cities. The text gives the firstborn spot as the reason.

The text says the opposite, friend. Verse 6 says Jehoram "…did evil in the sight of the LORD." He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. He also married a daughter of Ahab.

That's right. Verse 6 says Jehoram "…did evil in the sight of the LORD." He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done, and he married a daughter of Ahab. So the answer is False, because the text says he did evil, not right.

Yes, baker. Verse 7 says the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David "…because of the covenant He had made with David…" The verse also gives His promise to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. So the reason is what God had promised, not how Jehoram was acting.

The text never says a word about an army here. Verse 7 gives the reason: "…because of the covenant He had made with David…" The verse also gives His promise to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever.

Nothing in this passage mentions Jehoram praying, friend. Verse 7 says the LORD was unwilling to destroy the house of David "…because of the covenant He had made with David…" The verse also gives His promise to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever. Both reasons come from what God had said to David.

Right, baker. Verse 8 says Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and "…appointed their own king." They didn't just rebel, they put someone in charge of their own. This happened in the days of Jehoram.
Not a prophet, friend. Verse 8 says Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and "…appointed their own king." The verse names a king, not a prophet. This happened in the days of Jehoram.
Good guess, but it's a king. Verse 8 says Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and appointed their own king. No priest shows up in that verse.
That's right, baker. Verse 9 says Jehoram crossed into Edom with his officers and all his chariots. Not just some of the chariots, all of them.
Actually, it's true, friend. Verse 9 says Jehoram crossed into Edom with his officers and all his chariots. He went over with his officers and every one of his chariots.

Yes, baker. Verse 9 says that when the Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, he rose up and attacked by night. Surrounded, and he got up and went at them in the dark. I would've stayed seated and asked everybody to be reasonable.

No surrender in this one, friend. Verse 9 says that when the Edomites surrounded him, Jehoram "…rose up and attacked by night." He was surrounded and he chose to move. The text doesn't give us a white flag anywhere.

That's the reason, baker. Verse 10 says Libnah rebelled against his hand at the same time "…because Jehoram had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers." The text puts the reason right in the same verse.

You got it, baker. Verse 12 says a letter came to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet. It opens with "…This is what the LORD, the God of your father David, says…" So the message came as a letter, and it speaks for the LORD.

It's not a vision, baker. Verse 12 says a letter came to Jehoram from Elijah the prophet. The text names a letter, not a vision. I'd have guessed something fancier myself, but I bake by what the verse says.
